name: Waiter Curl
description: The waiter curl is performed by holding a weight plate by its rim with both hands underneath, palms facing upward as if carrying a tray. The underhand plate position keeps constant supination tension on the biceps throughout the curl, emphasizing the short head and brachialis. It is a simple, low-setup bicep exercise that also challenges the forearms and wrist stability.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a weight plate by the rim with both hands underneath, palms facing up. Elbows at the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose a plate with a comfortable grip around the rim. A 10-25kg plate works well for most lifters.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended, plate hanging below, palms supinated.
Step 2: Curl the plate upward by flexing the elbows, keeping the palms facing up throughout.
Step 3: Curl until maximum elbow flexion, keeping the plate horizontal.
Step 4: Lower slowly back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to assist the curl
safety_considerations: Ensure a firm grip on the plate rim before beginning
coaching_cues: Palms face the ceiling the whole way
